gp.text: Cost of Services and Gross Profit. Cost of services increased by $2.6 million for the thirteen weeks ended October 3, 2026, compared with the comparable prior-year period, primarily due to higher revenue. The cost of services as a percentage of revenue for the thirteen weeks ended October 3, 2026, and September 27, 2025, was 72.8% and 72.4%, respectively. See Segment Discussion for further information regarding changes in cost of services and gross profit.

oi.text: The following unaudited tables present the Company's GAAP net income and GAAP operating income, and the corresponding adjustments used to calculate Adjusted operating income, EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted net income, and adjusted diluted net earnings per share for the thirteen and thirty-nine weeks ended October 3, 2026, and September 27, 2025.

ga.text: Selling, General and Administrative. Selling, general, and administrative (“SGA”) expenses were $14.8 million for the thirteen weeks ended October 3, 2026, compared with $14.9 million for the comparable prior-year period. As a percentage of revenue, SGA expenses were 20.2% for the thirteen weeks ended October 3, 2026, compared to 21.3% for the comparable prior-year period. See Segment Discussion for further information on SGA expense changes.

sga.text: Selling, General and Administrative. Selling, general, and administrative (“SGA”) expenses were $14.8 million for the thirteen weeks ended October 3, 2026, compared with $14.9 million for the comparable prior-year period. As a percentage of revenue, SGA expenses were 20.2% for the thirteen weeks ended October 3, 2026, compared to 21.3% for the comparable prior-year period. See Segment Discussion for further information on SGA expense changes.

prov.text: This Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations is based on our consolidated financial statements, which have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“U.S. GAAP”). The preparation of financial statements in conformity with U.S. GAAP requires us to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and the reported amount of revenue and expenses during the reporting period. In our consolidated financial statements, estimates are used for, but not limited to, accounts receivable, contract assets, provision for credit losses, goodwill, long-lived intangible assets, accounting for stock options and restricted stock and stock unit awards, litigation or other contingent accruals, accounting for income taxes, and accrued bonuses. The various estimates and assumptions taken into account include, but are not limited to:

tax.text: Differences between the effective tax rate and the applicable U.S. federal statutory rate may arise, primarily from the effect of state and local income taxes, share-based compensation, and potential tax credits available to the Company. The actual 2026 effective tax rate may vary from the estimate depending on the actual operating income earned in various jurisdictions, the potential availability of tax credits, the vesting of share-based awards, and the amount of any permanent book-to-tax differences.

net.text: The following unaudited tables present the Company's GAAP net income and GAAP operating income, and the corresponding adjustments used to calculate Adjusted operating income, EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted net income, and adjusted diluted net earnings per share for the thirteen and thirty-nine weeks ended October 3, 2026, and September 27, 2025.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text:
Operating activities provided $9.8 million of cash for the thirty-nine weeks ended October 3, 2026, compared to $7.5 million in the comparable prior-year period. The major components of cash provided by operating activities in the thirty-nine weeks ended October 3, 2026, and the comparable prior-year period are as follows: net income, changes in accounts receivable and contract assets, the net of transit accounts payable and transit accounts receivable, prepaid expenses and other current assets, accounts payable and accrued expenses, accrued payroll and related costs, and deferred revenue.

For the thirty-nine weeks ended October 3, 2026, the Company reported net income of $11.5 million compared to $10.2 million for the comparable prior-year period. An increase in accounts receivable and contract assets in the thirty-nine weeks ended October 3, 2026, used $3.5 million of cash compared to $5.2 million in the comparable prior-year period.

wc.text: The Company’s corporate SGA expense includes but is not limited to the following costs: public company-related, executive compensation, board compensation, directors’ and officers’ insurance, SAP ERP infrastructure, numerous centralized functions including accounting and financial management, information technology and cyber security infrastructure, payroll, billing, accounts receivable, and marketing. The corporate segment team primarily operates out of the United States, with limited operations in Serbia and the Philippines. Corporate SGA expense was $4.4 million for both the thirteen weeks ended October 3, 2026, and the comparable prior-year period.

capex.text: Investing activities used $0.5 million to purchase property and equipment in the current period, compared with $1.4 million in the comparable prior-year period. The primary reason for the decrease was the completion of the Company’s new ERP software implementation in fiscal 2025.

Health Care.heading: Specialty Health Care
Health Care.text: Specialty Health Care revenue of $33.7 million for the thirteen weeks ended October 3, 2026, increased 12.4%, or $3.7 million, compared to the comparable prior-year period. The increase was primarily driven by the Company’s school clients, offset by a decrease in revenue from the Company’s non-school clients. Revenue from school clients for the thirteen weeks ended October 3, 2026, was $28.5 million, compared with $24.4 million for the comparable prior-year period. The increase in revenue from school contracts was driven by both existing and new clients. Revenue from non-school clients for the thirteen weeks ended October 3, 2026, was $5.2 million, compared to $5.6 million for the comparable prior-year period. Gross profit decreased by 4.4%, or $0.4 million, to $8.6 million for the thirteen weeks ended October 3, 2026, compared with $9.0 million in the comparable prior-year period. Gross profit decreased due to a decrease in gross profit margin. Gross profit margin for the thirteen weeks ended October 3, 2026, decreased to 25.5% from 30.0% in the comparable prior-year period. The decrease in gross profit margin was primarily attributed to a mix shift towards lower-margin services, slower-than-typical summer school assignments, and normal quarterly fluctuations.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

During the fiscal year ended December 28, 2024, the Company had two customers exceed 10% of consolidated revenue, representing 19.5 % and 14.1 % of consolidated revenue, respectively.
All customers exceeding 10% of consolidated revenue during the periods presented are included in the Company’s Specialty Health Care segment.
The Company’s five , ten and twenty largest customers accounted for approximately 48.5 %, 60.1 % and 70.6 %, respectively, of the Company’s revenue for the fiscal year ended December 28, 2024.
The Company’s operations depend on the continued efforts of its officers and other executive management.
The Company also depends on the performance and productivity of its local managers and field personnel.

The Company’s success depends on its ability to obtain and maintain its intellectual property, prevent its misappropriation or infringement, maintain trade secret protection, and conduct operations without violating or infringing on the intellectual property rights of third parties.

The Company is committed to optimizing its business model as a single-source premier provider of business and technology solutions with a strong vertical focus, offering an integrated suite of services through a global delivery platform.
The Company experiences volatility in its daily cash flow and, at times, relies on the revolving line of credit to provide daily liquidity for the Company’s financial operations.

The purchase plan permits eligible employees to purchase shares of common stock through payroll deductions for up to 10 % of qualified compensation, subject to maximum purchases in any one fiscal year of 3,000 shares.
